scope: Independent fictional tasks. Answer using the supplied artifacts and applicable skills; do not operate devices or modify any project. Numeric values belong only to these fixtures.

cases.request: Choose the primary workflow and diagnose why this arm solver stalls. Recommend the smallest justified correction and its acceptance checks.

artifacts.model: Seven revolute joints, fixed base; goal is end-effector position in base coordinates. Orientation is unconstrained.
artifacts.runtime: Jacobian is 3 by 7. The implementation computes an unconstrained DLS step then clips each joint to the position and per-cycle motion bounds.
artifacts.probe: At one active joint bound, this method repeats a 4.2 mm residual. An independently checked seed reaches 0.02 mm for the same target within the same bounds. Numerical FK derivatives agree with the 3 by 7 Jacobian.
artifacts.scope: Offline diagnosis and recommendation only. No device operation is requested. No prior approach record was supplied.

cases.request: Assess whether this mapping candidate meets the requested non-regression criterion, and identify the next focused investigation.

artifacts.mapping: A camera provides 17 named landmarks in camera-frame centimetres. A six-actuator gripper uses its own joint mapping in radians. Adapter conversions and labels have independent fixtures.
artifacts.criterion: Improve finger shape while keeping final model endpoint separation within 0.8 mm of the baseline during closing, including rapid approaches.
artifacts.results: The candidate's optimizer proposal meets that criterion. After a thumb filter and componentwise rate limiting, 11 of 240 closing samples increase separation by 3 to 6 mm. Both candidates satisfy all individual joint bounds.
artifacts.comparison: Same recording, original receipts, separate state histories, same initial/reset state and limits. The shape objective is the intended difference. No measured contact data is available.

cases.request: Can this fitted articulated model replace the current model? Give a bounded diagnosis and the most informative next validation.

artifacts.fit: Joint states, two link lengths and sensor mounting are estimated jointly from a single-axis movement. Fitted sensor-position RMS is 0.3 mm.
artifacts.alternatives: Three initializations produce lengths [5, 71], [22, 53] and [39, 36] mm, all with RMS between 0.3 and 0.4 mm. Their internal joint trajectories differ substantially. One mounting angle hits its bound.
artifacts.evaluation: The first half of one hold was fitted; its adjacent second half is called independent validation. An untrained flexion trial moves the wrong internal joint. No independent link-length measurement exists.
artifacts.scope: Raw input and current model are immutable. Candidate publication needs functional-motion improvement without loss of the protected poses.

cases.request: Review this proposed recovery handler against the supplied controller contract and describe the necessary correction.

artifacts.contract: A source-only gap with fresh feedback permits retaining the last admitted target. Feedback expiry requires the device's stop-and-disable procedure. A STOP-class drive fault latches motion prohibition, including new HOLD commands, until explicit recovery. An uncertain disable retains ownership for cleanup.
artifacts.handler: For source gap, feedback expiry, or drive fault: send(last_valid_target); clear_error_when_next_packet_is_finite(); release_owner_on_cleanup_timeout().
artifacts.scope: Read-only code review; no live process or device changes.

cases.request: Evaluate the freshness policy and the claim that this system guarantees a one-millisecond response.

artifacts.events: Input epoch A sequence 80 has host receipt 10.000 s. Epoch B sequence 1 is accepted at 10.050 s. A result for A:80 finishes at 10.080 s. A display loop republishes cached results and replaces their source receipt with current host time.
artifacts.measurements: Per-frame compute median is 0.8 ms and maximum is 15 ms. A simulation reaches the geometric goal after 84 frames at a declared simulated rate of 120 Hz. No actuator feedback was collected.
artifacts.contract: A new epoch resets accepted solver history. Repeated transport messages must retain source identity and age. The display loop is latest-only.

cases.request: Using these artifacts, decide whether the stated software-interface acceptance criterion is met. Identify any limits on that conclusion.

artifacts.criterion: The adapter emits the documented six-element command with correct ordering, units and source identity, and rejects non-finite values and wrong dimensions. Physical tracking is outside this acceptance criterion.
artifacts.evidence: An inspected source diff and configuration agree with a revision-matched test report. The report exercises each named criterion with a fake publisher and includes the command payloads and rejection results. All pass. No hardware was connected.
artifacts.context: Ordinary engineering conversation with no formal team approval protocol.

cases.request: The replay looked stable, so can we double the position gain and report this gripper's 0.6 effort as 0.6 N? Recommend the next useful check.

artifacts.interface: A position-target servo exposes a normalized vendor gain. Its inner-loop behavior is undocumented. The SDK effort field is motor current scaled by a placeholder Kt=1.
artifacts.replay: A fake publisher recorded the generated commands but did not simulate actuator dynamics or produce measured feedback. No transmission/friction model or load calibration is available.

cases.request: Choose whether any robotics domain skill is needed for this task: change a robot dashboard's button label from 'Start' to 'Preview'. The click handler, enabled state, device control and layout must remain unchanged. Explain the minimum validation.

artifacts.location: A single localization string used by the dashboard button; the task is a text edit with no runtime behavior change.
